question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must invoke a Python script that alerts the operations team when the router DC-RTR-1 becomes unreachable. Which configuration set accomplishes this task?
context:
Topology: DC-RTR-1 (10.19.31.1) connects to N9K-DC-1-SPINE-1 (10.19.31.2) and N9K-DC-1-SPINE-2 (10.19.31.3).
switch(config)# ip sla 10
switch(config-ip-sla)# icmp-echo 10.19.31.1
switch(config)# ip sla schedule 10 life forever start-time now
switch(config)# track 5 ip sla 10 reachability
imageNote: Diagram: DC-RTR-1 (10.19.31.1) connects to N9K-DC-1-SPINE-1 (10.19.31.2) and N9K-DC-1-SPINE-2 (10.19.31.3), which are linked to each other; includes the ip sla / track CLI configuration.
options: event scheduler name DOWN-ROUTER event track 2 state 1 not up event action 1.0 command source routerdown.py event start 0:00 repeat 0:05
track 3 ip sla 10 reachability event name GATEWAY-DOWN event state down action cli command routerdown.py
event manager applet ROUTER-DOWN-SLA event track 5 state down action 1.0 event-default action 2.0 cli command source routerdown.py
scheduler job name ROUTER-DOWN job track 9 state down action 1.0 cli source routerdown.py schedule 10
theory: Once IP SLA and a track object are already monitoring reachability to DC-RTR-1, EEM is the component that reacts to a change in that track object's state; an applet with 'event track 5 state down' fires the moment the tracked object transitions down, and an action such as 'cli command source routerdown.py' then sources/runs the Python alert script. The Scheduler and the other pseudo-syntax options aren't valid ways to bind an EEM/track event directly to invoking a script. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools) / (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
